newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Britain denies vetoing EU racism centre.
newsitem.headline: Britain denies vetoing EU racism centre.

text.p: Britain denied on Monday that it had vetoed plans to set up a European Union centre to collect data about racism and xenophobia, saying it only objected to creating it under the proposed EU treaty provision.

"The United Kingdom fully supports the creation of a European Monitoring Centre on Racism and Xenophobia and wants such a centre to be as effective as possible," Home Office minister Timothy Kirkhope told an anti-racism conference, according to a statement distributed in Brussels.

British diplomats in Brussels, rebutting a newspaper report that London had vetoed the centre, said Britain wanted EU governments to set up the centre by striking a deal amongst themselves rather than using Article 235 of the EC Treaty as proposed.
It argues that Article 235 -- which refers to action needed to achieve "one of the objectives of the Community" -- does not give the EU competence to set up such a centre.
It should be created outside of the EU treaty altogether, or at least under the EU's "Third Pillar" procedures applying to justice and home affairs questions, London says.
Acting outside of the treaty would allow the centre to collect information on racially motivated crime -- an area excluded from the current proposal, the diplomats said.
A Dutch diplomat who chairs the group that is thrashing out the proposal for the centre said he was unaware of any British veto. "I've never heard them say no," he told Reuters.
He said several questions had to be settled before the centre could be set up, in areas such as personnel and financing. "But the whole atmosphere is cooperative," he said.
He noted that all EU heads of state and governments, including British Prime Minister John Major, had endorsed the centre at European Councils, most recently last December in Dublin.

The European Commission's proposal calls on the centre to supply EU institutions and national governments with objective data on racism, xenophobia and anti-Semitism and set up a European Racism and Xenophobia Information Network.
Article 235 requires unanimous approval of EU governments.
